newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats output normal after more killings.
newsitem.headline: Amplats output normal after more killings.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd said its mines were operating normally on Monday despite further killings over the weekend.

Although the mines were quiet on Monday -- in the wake of the murder of two National Union of Mineworkers officials and four of their family members -- Amplats said it wanted visible policing and planned to meet with government ministers.
The weekend killings are the latest in a wave of violence that first wracked Amplats' three platinum mines last May.

"This has been going on for a while...Production has not been affected at all but it is a very, very worrying thing. We see people being brutally murdered on a regular basis," Amplats spokesman Johan Adler told Reuters.

A NUM official and three family members, including a child, were shot dead on Friday when unknown attackers stormed their house in the Eastern Cape. The official had gone there to organise the funeral of an Amplats worker murdered in June.
On Saturday another NUM official and his son were killed in a hostel at the Rustenburg section of Amplats' Rustenburg Platinum Mines Ltd (Rusplats).
Rusplats, the world's largest platinum mine, has been plagued by a long-running dispute over union representation. It was hit in late May by a two-day wildcat strike.
This weekend's murders shattered a peace accord signed on July 1 between labour unions at the mines aimed at halting sporadic outbreaks of violence.
Adler said Amplats planned to approach several ministers on Monday to urge more high profile policing at the mines.

"We're taking it up with the highest levels of government today. On Friday we asked for policing to be upped and even get the army in if needed. We need visible policing. The NUM requested it as well," he said.
Amplats' mines, including Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd and Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd, are situated in the Northern and North West provinces.

The Safety and Security MECs (members of executive council) in those provinces told the NUM on Friday that they too would approach national government as they believed the violence had become a national issue.
Adler declined to speculate on the cause of the violence. "I don't know what it's about. It doesn't seem to be a labour issue. It's not aimed at management or at production," he said.
But speculation in the local press blames the killings on conflict between the NUM and the Mouthpiece Workers' Union.
In May members of the Mouthpiece Workers' Union tortured two NUM members after a "kangaroo court" (informal trial). Some of those involved in the torture were dismissed.
In June two senior NUM leaders were killed by unknown gangs at the Amandelbult and Union sections of Rusplats.
Amplats produces about 1.8 million ounes of platinum a year.
